candidates.statement: This guidance provides recommendations to sponsors regarding measurement of ovarian toxicity 51 using clinical measures and biomarkers of ovarian function in relevant cancer clinical trials that 52 enroll premenopausal adults. Specifically, this guidance applies in the cancer setting where life 53 expectancy based on tumor type is of a sufficient time where ovarian toxicities may be relevant. 54 Ovarian toxicity should be considered as a safety endpoint in trials including premenopausal 55 adults and should be considered an integral part of a drug 2 development program when the 56 intended therapy will be used in premenopausal adults. 57

candidates.statement: • Sponsors should assess ovarian toxicity in relevant clinical trials of anti-cancer agents 101 that enroll premenopausal adults with ovaries. 102 • Sponsors should evaluate ovarian function with the following clinical measures and 103 laboratory biomarkers: 104 o Gynecologic history: clinical gynecologic data including menstrual history (e.g., 105 date of last menstrual period, cycle length and duration of menstrual bleeding, and 106 prior history and cause of irregular cycles, if applicable), prior pregnancies, and 107 live births. 108 o Laboratory biomarkers: serum anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), serum follicle 109 stimulating hormone (FSH), and serum estradiol (E2) levels, preferably on days 110 3-5 of the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle. 111  The concomitant measurement of serum AMH, serum FSH, and serum E2 112 in the early follicular phase provides the most comprehensive information 113 regarding the ovarian effects of exposure to anti-cancer therapies, and 114 potential reversibility of impaired ovarian function. 115 i) Sponsors should specify during trial design the type of assay used to measure AMH, 116 FSH, and E2 and a standardized laboratory methodology across sites is preferable. 117
